title: Aralo compatibility table `apps.toml` (format v0)
description: How the injector puts text into each app: the insert method, the delays, the undo style and the delete strategy, by bundle ID. Every app gets `defaults`; an `app` entry lists only what differs. The file is TOML; this schema describes it once parsed. Unlike a library file, an unknown key is an error, so that a typo cannot pass in silence. Format v0 is pre-release and may change without a migration.
$comment: Mirrors `File`, `App` and `Overrides` in crates/aralo-core/src/compat.rs; the table that ships is data/compat/apps.toml. Two rules are outside what a schema can say: bundle IDs are compared without regard to ASCII case, and no two entries may share one. When this file and the Rust types disagree, the Rust code wins; please report it.

version.description: The table format version. This schema describes version 0. A build refuses a table whose `version` is newer than it understands and keeps the one it has.

revision.description: This edition of the table, raised by one in every change to the file. A downloaded table replaces the one in use only when its revision is higher, so an older signed table cannot replace a newer one. Left out, it is 0.

defaults.description: What every app gets unless its entry says otherwise. A setting left out here takes the value built into the core, which is the `default` given for it below.

app.description: One entry per app that needs naming, in any order. In TOML, a list of `[[app]]` tables.

name.description: What people call the app. For readers of the file and for the injection matrix report; never used to find the app.

bundle_id.description: The app's bundle identifier, for example `com.apple.Terminal`.

insert.description: `auto`: type text up to `typing_limit`, paste longer text and anything with a line break. `type`: always type; a line break is sent as a Return key, and an expansion that pressed Return offers no undo. `paste`: always paste.

typing_limit.description: The longest text `auto` still types, in UTF-16 units.

key_delay_ms.description: Pause after every synthetic key, in milliseconds. Apps drop events that arrive faster than they read them.

paste_settle_ms.description: How long the app gets to read the pasteboard before the user's clipboard is put back, in milliseconds.

undo.description: `native`: a pasted expansion is one undo step in the app, so one Cmd+Z takes it back. `backspace`: every expansion is taken back with the delete strategy, for apps whose own undo cannot be trusted.

delete.description: `backspace`: one Backspace per character. `select`: Shift+Left over the characters, then one Backspace.
